description: The Pipeline Emergency Response Guidelines are a 52-page booklet for fire, police and other emergency responders on how to act at pipeline incidents, published in a 2022 edition by the Pipeline Association for Public Awareness, a nonprofit set up by pipeline operators to improve public safety. It opens with an incident response checklist (approach from upwind, uphill or upstream; secure the scene; identify hazards from pipeline markers and the DOT Emergency Response Guidebook; assess the situation; obtain help from the operator; protect people, property and the environment; work in unified command with the operator), and gives product hazard details for the commodities carried in pipelines, guidance on when to shelter in place or evacuate, safety when working over pipelines, what responders can expect from operators, and free training resources. Coverage: pipelines in the United States. Access: free PDF, printed copies free to response agencies on request. Licence and cost: free, copyright of the association with reproduction by request. Caveats: generic guidance written by industry; it gives no incident data, and local operator plans take precedence. It helps set response actions, isolation distances and roles in emergency response scenarios for pipeline failures. It relates to the PHMSA incident data and the National Pipeline Mapping System in the catalogue.
